title: SDV Snippet Document
description: A snippet document is valid JSON. Every value is a STRING_VALUE: either a string literal or a single-key function call (an object with exactly one $-key). Evaluation is a tree-walk; every node evaluates to a string. The interpreter is sdv_snippets.py; the grammar is snippets_syntax.txt.

$schema.description: Optional pointer to this schema, for editor tooling. Ignored by the interpreter.

$basedir.description: Base directory for relative paths, resolved relative to the document's own directory. Usually a string literal such as ".".

$comment: The root is a statement list: the interpreter iterates its keys, skips $schema and $basedir, and evaluates each remaining {$fn: params} in order. In practice a document declares $basedir and one $write.

stringValue.description: Either a string literal or a function call that returns a string.

functionCall.description: An object with exactly one $-key naming the function; its value holds the named parameters.

readParams.description: $read: read the file at path and return its contents as a string (trailing newlines stripped).

path.description: Path to the file, relative to $basedir unless absolute.

writeParams.description: $write: create (truncate) the file at path, write content followed by one newline, and return content.

path.description: Destination path, relative to $basedir unless absolute.

replaceParams.description: $replace: in content, replace each literal token from rules with its value, applied in order.

rules.description: Map of literal token -> replacement string. A token absent from content is a harmless no-op.

switchParams.description: $switch: evaluate cond, then return the value of the case whose literal key equals it. No matching case raises an error.

cond.description: The string to test against the case labels, e.g. {"$opt":{"arg":"--target"}}.

cases.description: Map of literal label -> string value returned when cond equals that label.

optParams.description: $opt: return the value of the named command-line option (e.g. --target). Unset option raises an error.

arg.description: The option name including leading dashes, e.g. "--target".

literalMap.description: Object mapping string literals to STRING_VALUEs. Keys are matched literally, never evaluated.
